A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, and complete Appendices A-C. Content can be matched reliably despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original synthetic experiments on neural-network sample complexity and MSE-versus-Huber feature learning, with outcomes in Figures 1-2.

after.justification: Section 6 retains the original synthetic experiments and their reported outcomes in Figures 1-2.

M1.justification: The two-layer architecture and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, including initialization, sample splitting, first-layer training, bias reinitialization, and second-layer training.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian-input synthetic tasks: a weighted quadratic target and h4(x1)+h4(x2). No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Section 6.2 retains the same MSE-versus-Huber comparison. Changes to cited theoretical predecessors do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains the same architectures, initialization, optimizer settings, sample-size sweeps, dimensions, and metrics. The first experiment still specifies width 4, Adam learning rate 0.005, up to 1000 epochs, and batch size 32.

E4.justification: The sample-complexity sweeps and loss-choice analysis are unchanged. Neither the main text nor the appendices add or remove ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five seeds for Figure 1 and medians with 30th and 70th percentiles over ten seeds for Figure 2. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The embedded plots in Figures 1-2 are identical, and their accompanying findings are retained: decreasing sample-size exponents with dimension and substantially better feature alignment with Huber than MSE.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorem statements, Corollary 3.1, derivations, and proofs in Appendices A-C are unchanged. Apparent equation differences in extraction resolve to spacing or reading-order differences.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1, and conclusion retain the same learning guarantees, near-optimal sample and time complexities, and requirement for more than constantly many first-layer training steps.

C2.justification: The power-iteration interpretation, stopping-time tradeoff, non-generative-staircase restriction, loss-selection explanation, and conjectured extension beyond Gaussian inputs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1, appendix hyperparameter prescriptions, and Section 6 implementation details are retained. No reproducibility settings or code/data access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds DIKR25 and discusses its agnostic PAC and uniform guarantees. The introduction identifies MW26, previously cited as MW25, instead of ADK+25 as the closest predecessor. The DH24 bibliography entry is removed. These are limited literature and positioning revisions.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes heading capitalization, renames 'Proof Sketch' and 'Conclusions and Future Works,' adds author affiliations, and makes localized wording and acknowledgement edits. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is regrouped with Section 6.1 and its discussion, while surrounding text and reference placement are reflowed. Both figures, their captions, axes, and legends remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added DIKR25 discussion clarifies distinctions between related learning guarantees, and the revised introduction better aligns with the existing Montanari-Wang comparison. More consistent headings and Figure 1 placement modestly improve readability. The method, proofs, and empirical evidence remain unchanged, limiting the overall gain.
